video_goal: Demonstrate the proper setup, pad placement, and activation of a TENS 7000 unit for lower back pain relief.
required_subjects_and_props: TENS 7000 unit, two lead wires, four square electrode pads, human subject with exposed lower back

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands place the silver TENS 7000 unit, two coiled lead wires, and four square electrode pads onto a flat wooden table.
Hands push the two plastic plugs of the lead wires firmly into the two circular ports located at the top edge of the TENS 7000 unit.
Fingers push the red and black metal pins at the ends of the lead wires into the short wire connectors attached to each of the four electrode pads.
Hands peel the clear plastic backing off the black, sticky side of the first square electrode pad.
A hand presses the first sticky pad onto the bare skin of the lower back, positioning it exactly two inches to the left of the spine.
The hand presses the second pad onto the skin, two inches to the right of the spine, directly parallel to the first pad.
The hand presses the third and fourth pads onto the lower back, positioning them two inches below the first two pads to form a square pattern around the lumbar region.
Fingers flip open the front plastic cover of the TENS 7000 unit to reveal the gray control buttons and the LCD screen.
Thumb and index finger twist the top left dial clockwise until a physical click occurs and the LCD screen illuminates with black text.
A finger presses the 'Mode' button below the screen, causing the text on the LCD display to cycle until the word 'Normal' appears.
Fingers slowly twist both top dials clockwise, stopping when the LCD screen displays the number '3' to indicate the rising intensity level.
The person slides the metal clip located on the back of the TENS 7000 unit securely onto the waistband of their pants.
